units.delivery: اتكلم بالمصري القاهري الطبيعي، كأنك مدرّس بيشرح لطلبة تعليم فني زراعي بهدوء ووضوح. الجيم مصرية زي G في gold، والقاف همزة في الكلمات اليومية اللّي المصريين بينطقوها كده. نبرة دافية وسرعة متوسّطة ووقفات طبيعية. راعي الشدّات من غير مبالغة أو تطويل. حافظ على كلّ النفي والشروط وحدود التدريب. اقرأ نصّ الإلقاء بسّ، من غير مقدّمة أو تعليق أو قراءة التعليمات. بلاش فصحى أو لهجة خليجية أو نبرة نشرات الأخبار. اشرح النص كله كجزء واحد متصل، من غير تمثيل شخصيات أو إضافة نصايح طبية.

sourceBindings.text: المادة الرملية ملمسها خشن، وغالبًا صرفها أسرع واحتفاظها بالمياه أقل. التربة الخشنة ممكن تسخن وتجف أسرع من تربة أدق وأرطب في ظروف مشابهة. ده قد يساعد بداية النمو أحيانًا، لكنه ممكن يخلي منطقة الجذور تفقد المياه أسرع. الطقس والمادة العضوية وطبقات التربة يغيروا النتيجة الفعلية.

كل أسماء المحاصيل في مقارنة الرمل الأصلية: الجزر والبطاطس والفجل والخس والفراولة والشمام والذرة. الجزر والفجل يوضحوا أهمية منطقة جذور مفككة ومن غير عوائق. البطاطس محتاجة منطقة جذور مناسبة وصرفًا ملائمًا برضه. ولا اسم منهم يبرر تجاهل إمداد المياه أو تحليل العناصر.

الخس والفراولة في الموقع الرملي يحتاجوا اهتمامًا خاصًا بثبات المياه المتاحة للجذور. الشمام والذرة احتمالان لو الموسم والمياه وإدارة العناصر مناسبين. الفكرة المشتركة مش إن الرمل فيه كل الغذاء اللي المحاصيل محتاجاه؛ الفكرة إن صرفه وسهولة خدمته ممكن يفيدوا مع إدارة محدودية الاحتفاظ.

ما تحولش كلمة 'رملي' إلى عدد ريات ثابت أو أمر بزيادة السماد من غير خطة. اربط الإدارة بالقياسات والمحصول. المياه الزائدة ممكن تغسل عناصر سريعة الحركة أسفل الجذور، وكمية السماد ما تتحددش من الملمس وحده.

أمثلة المحاصيل في المقارنة: الطماطم والفلفل والخيار والفاصوليا الخضراء والذرة. خضار ومحاصيل حقلية أخرى كثيرة قد تلائم التربة اللومية لو الشروط مناسبة. خلي الفئات الواسعة زي 'الخضار' و'المحاصيل الحقلية' دعوة للتحقق من احتياجات محصول محدد، مش حكمًا إن كل محصول هينجح.

للطماطم والفلفل اشرح دور منطقة جذور مهواة وإمداد مياه مدروس، وبعدها راجع الموسم والصنف ودرجة الحموضة والملوحة والعناصر المطلوبة. وللخيار والفاصوليا الخضراء استخدم نفس الاستدلال المبني على الدليل، بدل افتراض إن اسم القوام يضمن النجاح.

وجود نفس المحصول في قائمتين مش تناقض. الذرة قد تكون احتمالًا في التربة الرملية واللومية مع إدارة مختلفة للمياه والعناصر. الصلاحية تعتمد على اجتماع المحصول والتربة والإدارة، مش لعبة مطابقة اسم واحد باسم واحد.

A cultivar is a selected crop variety; its requirements can differ from those of another cultivar. State the actual site and cultivar before turning a teaching example into a farm plan.

For the comparisons below, assume the crop is in a suitable local season and the site is safe for food production. Treat each crop name as a candidate with conditions to verify, not a promise of success. Where information is missing, state the check needed instead of inventing a measurement.

sourceBindings.text: Sandy material feels gritty and commonly has relatively rapid drainage and low water retention. Coarse soils may warm and dry more quickly than comparable wetter fine soils. This can aid establishment in some conditions, but the root zone may also run short of water sooner. Weather, organic matter and soil layers still influence what happens.

The complete set of candidates in this comparison is carrots, potatoes, radishes, lettuce, strawberries, melons and corn. Carrots and radishes illustrate the value of a loose, unobstructed rooting zone. Potatoes also need a suitable rooting zone and drainage. None is a reason to neglect water supply or nutrient tests.

Lettuce and strawberries on a sandy site need particular attention to a reliable root-zone water supply. Melons and corn can be considered where season, water and nutrient management fit. The common reasoning is not that sand contains all the nutrients these crops need; it is that its drainage and workability may be useful while its retention limitations are managed.

Do not translate 'sandy' into 'irrigate a fixed number of times' or 'apply extra fertilizer' without a plan. Match management to measured conditions and the crop. Excess water can carry mobile nutrients below the root zone, and a fertilizer amount cannot be selected from feel alone.

sourceBindings.text: Clay-rich material is often sticky and mouldable when wet and can hold water and some nutrients well. It may have slow drainage or poor aeration where structure, compaction or the profile restrict water movement. Waterlogging means the soil remains excessively wet with limited air for roots; it is not a synonym for clay.

Candidates in the comparison are cabbage, broccoli, kale, wheat and fruit trees. Cabbage, broccoli and kale illustrate crops that can use a moisture-retentive soil when it remains sufficiently aerated and drained. Wheat also requires a suitable seasonal and site plan. 'Fruit trees' is a broad category: the species and rootstock must be specified before recommending a tree for an actual field.

Beans also appear among the clay-soil examples. Keep the example with a clear condition: suitable, well-drained soil, not persistent waterlogging. Different bean species have different needs; a common bean example does not justify the same advice for every bean crop. Do not claim that beans tolerate a saturated root zone merely because their name appears in a clay-soil list.

Clay can retain nutrients without being sufficiently fertile for the crop. Check the relevant test results. Protect structure and avoid unnecessary traffic or cultivation when conditions would smear and compact the soil. If drainage is inadequate, selecting a different vegetable name does not automatically solve the problem.

sourceBindings.text: Loam has a mixture of the mineral particle sizes within a texture range. Under suitable structure it can balance drainage, aeration and water retention. The name does not prove a high organic-matter content or a complete nutrient supply, and it does not identify a commercial potting medium.

Candidates in the comparison include tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, green beans and corn. Many other vegetables and field crops may suit loamy soil with the right conditions. Keep the broad categories 'vegetables' and 'field crops' as invitations to check a named crop's requirements, not a rule that every crop will thrive.

For tomatoes and peppers, explain how an aerated root zone with a managed water supply supports the choice; then verify season, cultivar, pH, salinity and nutrient needs. For cucumbers and green beans, use the same evidence-based reasoning rather than assuming the texture name guarantees success.

A crop appearing in more than one list is not a contradiction. Corn can be considered in sandy and loamy soils under different water and nutrient management. Suitability depends on the combination of crop, soil and management, rather than a one-to-one matching game.

sourceBindings.text: Imagine a grower planning carrots in a heavy, compacted bed that remains wet after irrigation. Carrots need room for their storage roots to develop. Dense clods, compaction or restricted drainage can lead to difficult rooting and poor root quality; persistent wetness also increases the risk of root problems.

First distinguish the problems. A clay-rich texture is one property; compaction and persistent wetness are additional site observations. Carrots are not automatically impossible in every clay soil. A well-drained, non-compacted finer soil can be suitable, depending on the cultivar and conditions.

Cabbage or broccoli can be discussed as alternatives in a moisture-retentive but adequately drained bed. Do not recommend either as a cure for standing water. If the site remains waterlogged, investigate and address that condition before endorsing the planting plan.

For the exit comparison, a sample makes a strong ribbon longer than 5 cm. Between carrots and cabbage, cabbage may be the more plausible candidate under a stated moisture-retentive, aerated and drained scenario. The ribbon alone cannot choose the crop. Explain what drainage, structure and other crop information you still need.

sourceBindings.text: For A, B and C, write two candidate crops after recording the actual texture result. For each candidate give a reason connected to a soil property and at least one condition to verify. You can choose a well-justified alternative; the task is not to guess one hidden crop name.

A sandy sample might lead to carrots and radishes where the bed is loose and the water supply is managed. A clay-rich sample might lead to cabbage and broccoli where drainage and aeration are adequate. A loamy sample might lead to tomatoes and peppers where season and test results fit. These are worked examples, not compulsory answers tied to A, B or C.

The workshop asks for two crops per sample. The separate practical process card asks for at least one per sample. Identify which one of your two is used as the evidence for that card; do not combine the two requirements into an invented score. The testing and cleaning observations from the previous step must also be present before that complete process card can be closed.

Discuss the part of the test that was hardest and how it affected confidence in your recommendation. Compare reasons with another learner, then explain one choice to the group. Revise a recommendation if the evidence changes while keeping the earlier record traceable.

A sandy sample might lead to carrots and radishes where the bed is loose and the water supply is managed. A clay-rich sample might lead to cabbage and broccoli where drainage and aeration are adequate. A loamy sample might lead to tomatoes and peppers where season and test results fit. These are worked examples, not compulsory answers tied to A, B or C.

The workshop asks for two crops per sample. The separate practical process card asks for at least one per sample. Identify which one of your two is used as the evidence for that card; do not combine the two requirements into an invented score. The testing and cleaning observations from the previous step must also be present before that complete process card can be closed.

Discuss the part of the test that was hardest and how it affected confidence in your recommendation. Compare reasons with another learner, then explain one choice to the group. Revise a recommendation if the evidence changes while keeping the earlier record traceable.

sourceBindings.text: Il materiale sabbioso è granuloso e spesso drena relativamente presto, trattenendo meno acqua. Un suolo grossolano può scaldarsi e asciugarsi più rapidamente di uno più fine e umido. In certi casi aiuta l'avvio della coltura, ma la zona radicale può rimanere senz'acqua prima. Clima, sostanza organica e strati del terreno contano comunque.

L'elenco completo di candidati nell'originale è carote, patate, ravanelli, lattuga, fragole, meloni e mais. Carote e ravanelli mostrano il valore di una zona radicale sciolta e senza ostacoli. Anche le patate richiedono spazio radicale e drenaggio adeguati. Nessuno di questi nomi giustifica trascurare acqua o analisi nutritive.

Lattuga e fragole in un sito sabbioso richiedono attenzione particolare a una fornitura affidabile d'acqua alle radici. Meloni e mais sono possibili se stagione, acqua e nutrizione sono gestite bene. La ragione comune non è che la sabbia contenga tutti i nutrienti necessari: drenaggio e lavorabilità possono aiutare, mentre i limiti di ritenzione vanno gestiti.

Non tradurre 'sabbioso' in un numero fisso di irrigazioni o in 'più fertilizzante' senza piano. Adatta la gestione a misure e coltura. Troppa acqua può trasportare nutrienti mobili sotto le radici; la dose di concime non si decide toccando il suolo.

sourceBindings.text: Il materiale ricco di argilla è spesso appiccicoso e modellabile da umido e può trattenere acqua e alcuni nutrienti. Può drenare lentamente e avere poca aerazione se struttura, compattazione o profilo limitano il movimento. Ristagno significa eccessiva bagnatura persistente e poco ossigeno per le radici; non è sinonimo di argilla.

I candidati originali sono cavolo, broccoli, cavolo riccio, frumento e alberi da frutto. I primi tre possono sfruttare una buona ritenzione d'acqua se il terreno resta sufficientemente aerato e drenato. Il frumento richiede un piano stagionale e di sito. 'Alberi da frutto' è un insieme vasto: prima di consigliare un impianto devi precisare specie e portinnesto.

Fra gli esempi argillosi compare anche il fagiolo. Mantieni l'esempio con una condizione chiara: terreno adatto e ben drenato, non ristagno continuo. Specie di fagiolo diverse hanno bisogni diversi; un esempio di fagiolo comune non vale per tutti. Non sostenere che tollerino radici sature solo perché compaiono nella lista.

L'argilla può trattenere nutrienti senza fornirne abbastanza alla coltura. Controlla le analisi pertinenti. Proteggi la struttura ed evita passaggi e lavorazioni inutili quando il suolo rischia di impastarsi e compattarsi. Se il drenaggio è insufficiente, scegliere un'altra verdura non risolve automaticamente il problema.

sourceBindings.text: Il franco è una miscela di dimensioni minerali entro un intervallo tessiturale. Con una buona struttura può bilanciare drenaggio, aerazione e ritenzione idrica. Il nome non dimostra molta sostanza organica né piena disponibilità di nutrienti, e non identifica automaticamente un terriccio commerciale.

I candidati sono pomodori, peperoni, cetrioli, fagiolini e mais. Molte altre verdure e colture di pieno campo possono adattarsi se le condizioni sono giuste. Le categorie generiche 'verdure' e 'colture di campo' invitano a controllare una coltura precisa, non affermano che tutte prosperino.

Per pomodori e peperoni spiega come zona radicale aerata e acqua gestita sostengano la scelta; poi verifica stagione, cultivar, pH, salinità e nutrienti. Applica lo stesso ragionamento a cetrioli e fagiolini, senza ritenere che il nome della tessitura garantisca successo.

Una coltura in due elenchi non è una contraddizione. Il mais può essere considerato su sabbia e franco con diversa gestione idrica e nutritiva. L'idoneità deriva dall'unione di coltura, suolo e gestione, non da un gioco di abbinamenti uno a uno.

sourceBindings.text: Immagina un agricoltore che vuole carote in un letto pesante e compattato che rimane bagnato dopo l'irrigazione. La radice di riserva della carota ha bisogno di spazio. Zolle dure, compattazione o drenaggio ristretto possono ostacolarne crescita e qualità; l'umidità persistente aumenta il rischio di problemi radicali.

Distingui i problemi: tessitura argillosa è una proprietà; compattazione e ristagno sono ulteriori osservazioni del sito. Le carote non sono impossibili in ogni argilla. Un suolo più fine ma ben drenato e non compattato può essere adatto, secondo cultivar e condizioni.

Cavolo o broccoli si possono discutere come alternative in un letto che conserva umidità ma drena e si aera abbastanza. Non proporli come cura dell'acqua stagnante. Se il sito resta allagato, indaga e affronta il problema prima di approvare l'impianto.

Nel confronto finale il campione forma un nastro forte oltre 5 cm. Fra carote e cavolo, il cavolo può essere più plausibile se specifichi suolo umido ma aerato e drenato. Il nastro da solo non sceglie la coltura. Spiega quali informazioni su drenaggio, struttura e coltura mancano ancora.

sourceBindings.text: Per A, B e C scrivi due colture candidate dopo aver registrato la tessitura reale. Per ciascuna indica un motivo legato al suolo e almeno una condizione da verificare. Puoi scegliere un'alternativa ben motivata: non devi indovinare un unico nome segreto.

Un campione sabbioso può suggerire carote e ravanelli con letto sciolto e acqua gestita; uno argilloso cavolo e broccoli con sufficiente drenaggio e aerazione; uno franco pomodori e peperoni con stagione e analisi adeguate. Sono esempi svolti, non risposte obbligatorie per le lettere A, B e C.

Il laboratorio chiede due colture per campione; la scheda pratica distinta ne chiede almeno una. Indica quale delle tue due soddisfa il minimo della scheda, senza fondere i requisiti in un punteggio inventato. Prima di chiudere l'intera scheda devono esserci anche le osservazioni dei test e della pulizia della fase precedente.

Discuti la parte più difficile della prova e come abbia influito sulla fiducia nella raccomandazione. Confronta le ragioni con un compagno, poi spiega al gruppo una scelta. Se cambia la prova, rivedi la raccomandazione mantenendo rintracciabile il registro precedente.

sourceBindings.text: Nimm dein Beobachtungsblatt der Bandprobe. Nutze den notierten Texturschluss, seine Belege und jede Unsicherheit. A, B oder C ist kein Bodentyp; die Reihenfolge kann wechseln. Ändere ein Messergebnis nicht, weil du eine bestimmte Kultur bevorzugst.

Textur beeinflusst Wasserbewegung, Wasserspeicherung, Belüftung und die Fähigkeit, manche Nährstoffe zurückzuhalten. Speicherfähigkeit bedeutet Schutz vor Verlust, nicht eine Messung der gerade pflanzenverfügbaren Menge. Tonreicher Boden kann mangelhaft versorgt sein, sandiger Boden bei passender Bewirtschaftung ausreichend.

Für eine Empfehlung zählen außerdem Drainage im Bodenprofil, Tiefe und Struktur, Salzgehalt, pH-Wert, Nährstoffanalysen, Bewässerungswasser, Temperatur und Jahreszeit. Eine Sorte ist eine ausgewählte Variante einer Kultur; ihre Ansprüche können sich von anderen Sorten unterscheiden. Benenne Standort und Sorte, bevor ein Lehrbeispiel zum Betriebsplan wird.

Für die Vergleiche nehmen wir eine geeignete örtliche Saison und einen Standort an, der sicher für Lebensmittelanbau ist. Jeder Pflanzenname ist ein Kandidat mit zu prüfenden Bedingungen, keine Erfolgsgarantie. Fehlen Angaben, nenne die nötige Prüfung statt eine Zahl zu erfinden.
